Welcome. This quick tour shows the five tabs of the app. You can skip it and open it again from Settings.
Connect to your node here: tap “Scan and connect” and choose it. Close the official Meshtastic app first. You also choose the ping mode: to the channel, or direct to one node.

“Start” sends pings automatically while you move; “Ping” sends one right away. Green means someone heard you, red means nobody did. “Layers” chooses what is drawn: heat map, cells, route, nearby gaps… Tap the card at the top to fold it; when a ping is not sent, it shows why. Press and hold on the map to see a cell’s sheet or delete measurements. Tap the legend to see what each colour means.

Three sections. Wardrives: choose which ones are shown, and rename, share, import or delete them. Analysis: summary, report, comparison, noise chart and the nodes within range. Export: map image, coverage files and offline maps. You can also filter by dates or show only the latest wardrive.
Everything that happens is written here. If something fails, copy the log to ask for help.

Settings are grouped by topic: ping, measurement (smart ping, pause when the channel is busy, node GPS), map, connection, privacy and language. Optional features are off by default. Every number has a line explaining it. New: theme (night mode), ping by speed and the criterion for good or bad pings.

Distance: %2$s km

Best SNR: %10$s dB

• Heard by the mesh: your node heard a neighbour rebroadcast your ping (implicit ACK).
• ACK from target: in direct mode, the target node confirmed it.
• No response: nothing arrived within the maximum wait.
• Relay: last byte of the ID of the node that rebroadcast; the app lists the known nodes that match.
• SNR and RSSI: measured by your node when it heard the reply, so they describe the path towards you.
• Noise floor (NF): estimated from each packet heard: RSSI − SNR if the SNR is positive, the RSSI itself if negative. Packets with SNR above 5 dB are left out.
• Map colours: green SNR ≥ −7 dB, amber −7 to −13 dB, orange below −13 dB, red no response.
• Cells: squares of the size set in Settings, coloured by their best SNR.
• Success %: answered ÷ (answered + no response).
• Conditions and difficulty: dB compared with a stock 2 dBi antenna outside the vehicle at 22 dBm (pocket −15, bag −10, hand −3, inside car −8, dashboard −5, roof 0, mast +3; plus antenna gain −2 and power −22). ≥ −3 easy, ≥ −10 normal, below hard.
• Weighted criterion: replies always count. Failures with «hard» conditions are «unconfirmed». Each cell takes the state of its latest outing with conclusive data; ▲/▼ mark changes.
• Late reply: if it arrives more than 75 m from where it was sent, the success is placed where it arrived.
• Estimate: inverse-distance average of measured cells within 2 km, confidence by distance and number of neighbours; with relief, line of sight to the nodes that heard you (raises it if clear, halves it if a hill blocks).

MeshWardrive does not collect any data. It has no servers or accounts, no analytics or advertising, and sends nothing to the author or to third parties. Your measurements stay on your phone and only leave it if you export or share them.

What does leave the phone:
• Pings go out over the radio and anyone with the channel can read them, including your coordinates if you enable that option.
• With the online map, the OpenStreetMap servers receive your IP address and the area you are viewing. With an offline map, they don’t.

Data from other nodes (names, positions, relays) arrives over the radio and is not verified: anyone can fake it.

If you download the relief for the coverage map, the Terrain Tiles server (AWS) sees which area is requested, as with any web map.

Smooth colours: what you measured (green to orange: coverage by SNR; red: no coverage with reliable conditions; grey-blue: only failures with poor conditions).

Hatched cells: estimate where you have not measured, never mixed up with real data. It interpolates nearby measured cells (up to 2 km) and, if you download the relief, checks whether a hill blocks the view to the nodes that heard you. Cells with low confidence are not shown.

It is downloaded only for the area you are viewing (open Terrain Tiles data, about 30 m per pixel) and then works offline. The server sees which area is requested, as with any web map; your position is never sent.

Data → Analysis → «Coverage map» opens a screen to look things up: heat map without points, a hatched estimate where you have not measured, and a sheet for each cell (tap it). The «Relief» button downloads the terrain of the area so the estimate can take hills into account.
